content: Netflix is making monetization a top priority amid reports of falling viewing time. As part of its third-quarter earnings report on Tuesday, Netflix lists improvements to monetization as one of its main focuses going forward, alongside efforts to boost entertainment value and leverage new technology. The streaming giant doesn’t say exactly how it plans to improve its monetization, but the company notes that these goals will help Netflix “create member value that lets us occasionally raise prices, and increase advertiser demand.” Netflix also highlighted plans to push further into original titles, live events, and third-party programming as it faces an “intense competition and an explosion of content competing for consumer attention.” An analysis from financial firm Jefferies estimated that Netflix’s monthly viewing time per member dropped to 49 hours in the first half of this year, down from 66 hours in the first half of 2023, according to a report from Reuters. At the same time, Netflix made up 7.8 percent of US viewing time in the US in July, a one-percentage-point dip from the same time last year, The New York Times reports. During an earnings call, Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos pointed to success abroad when answering a question about the company’s content strategy. “We see titles across Latin America, EMEA (Europe, the Middle East and Africa), APAC (Asia-Pacific), driving engagement, subscriber growth, revenue, and profit,” Sarandos said. “Now, the US is also working. It’s just not growing as fast as it could or as fast as we’d like.” Last week, Netflix laid off around 1,000 employees, while replacing key executives, including chief content officer Bela Bajaria and film head Dan Lin. Former Disney executive Peter Rice is taking over as chief content officer on October 26th. The Wall Street Journal recently reported that Netflix co-CEO Ted Sarandos complained internally that US-based users have been spending less time on the service, and that it’s “short on new hit shows.” In its letter to investors, Netflix mentions its upcoming lineup of NFL games, its Grand Theft Auto VI preview, and its partnership with French TV station TF1 as evidence of opening its platform to a wider breadth of content. The company reported earning $12.9 billion over the past few months, marking a 12 percent year-over-year increase. It also plans to bring its ad-supported tier — which raked in $1.5 billion last year — to 15 new countries in 2027. In the coming months, Netflix may be facing tougher competition from HBO Max and Paramount Plus following the Skydance megamerger, as co-CEO David Ellison has said that he plans to combine the two apps into a single service. The streamer struck deals with several creators as it competes with YouTube, which has reportedly offered channels “millions of dollars” not to post their videos on Netflix. Netflix has also weighed making even bigger changes to its app, including integrating other third-party streamers, such as Peacock and Fox One, as well as adding always-on channels, according to reports from The New York Times and The Wall Street Journal. Update, October 20th: Added a quote from Sarandos.

chineseContent: 有报道称，观看时间不断减少，Netflix 将盈利作为首要任务。作为周二第三季度收益报告的一部分，Netflix 将改善货币化列为其未来的主要关注点之一，同时努力提高娱乐价值和利用新技术。这家流媒体巨头没有具体说明计划如何提高其盈利能力，但该公司指出，这些目标将帮助 Netflix“创造会员价值，让我们偶尔提高价格，并增加广告商的需求。” Netflix 还强调了进一步推进原创作品、现场活动和第三方节目的计划，因为它面临着“激烈的竞争和争夺消费者注意力的内容爆炸”。据路透社报道，金融公司 Jefferies 的分析估计，今年上半年 Netflix 的每位会员每月观看时间从 2023 年上半年的 66 小时下降至 49 小时。与此同时，据《纽约时报》报道，Netflix 占美国 7 月观看时间的 7.8%，比去年同期下降了 1 个百分点。在财报电话会议上，Netflix 联合首席执行官特德·萨兰多斯 (Ted Sarandos) 在回答有关公司内容策略的问题时指出了在海外取得的成功。 “我们看到拉丁美洲、EMEA（欧洲、中东和非洲）、APAC（亚太地区）的游戏都在推动参与度、用户增长、收入和利润，”萨兰多斯说。 “现在，美国也在发挥作用。它的增长速度没有达到应有的速度，也没有达到我们希望的速度。”上周，Netflix 解雇了约 1000 名员工，同时更换了主要高管，包括首席内容官贝拉·巴贾里亚 (Bela Bajaria) 和电影主管丹·林 (Dan Lin)。迪士尼前高管彼得·赖斯 (Peter Rice) 将于 10 月接任首席内容官
